newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex called lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex called lower on profit-taking.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex was seen pulled down by profit-taking early Friday on overextended heating oil prices which were called lower after hitting fresh post-Gulf War highs Thursday, traders said.
"There is really no fresh buying coming in, and there are a lot of longs that are taking profits," said a trader.

Heating oil and gasoline were called 0.25 cent to 0.50 cent lower while crude oil was called 15 to 20 cents lower. "Heat finally broke 72.25 yesterday after its third attempt, but it really had to struggle to go higher after that," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Energy Group.
Traders said heating oil could enter a short-term correction where it shaves off as much as two cents.
On Thursday, heating oil settled 0.87 cent lower at 70.90 cents a gallon after rising as high as 72.80 cents, breaking the post-Gulf War high of 72.25 made the week of November 8, 1991.

October gasoline settled down 0.11 cent to 62.99 cents a gallon, and November crude settled off 30 cents at 24.16 cents a barrel. Refco's Yu said short-term profit-taking in heating oil could shave as much as $1.00 off the price of crude, though he said the market remains bullish longer term.
For the past several months, heating oil's price has ascended steeply on tight supplies in the United States and Europe.
Futures of gas oil, the European equivalent of heating oil, tumbled Friday on profit-taking on London's IPE after having made five-year highs.
October gas oil on the IPE was off $5.25 a tonne at $226.50.
"It's (the tight supplies) been factored in as much as it can be at this point," said Yu.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
